112.55000,37.87000.desc: A medical institution approved by China's National Health Commission to perform assisted reproduction. Approved for: ICSI — a single sperm injected into the egg; IVF with embryo transfer; embryo screening before transfer; insemination with donor sperm; insemination with the partner's sperm. All of its approvals are in formal operation. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Approval is compulsory in China and performing assisted reproduction without it is unlawful, so this list is a register rather than a directory of members. It names every approved institution in the country, which is more than almost any other state publishes. The address did not geocode, so this point sits at the centre of the province rather than at the institution.

11.61970,44.83780.name: Illumina Italy / Ferrara sequencing hub
11.61970,44.83780.desc: A large European sequencing operation, and part of how genomic capacity spread beyond a handful of national centres. Where sequencing can be done cheaply determines who can check things — what is in a seed lot, a food shipment, a wild population — which makes distributed capacity one of the few developments on this map that helps the people doing the checking.

11.61970,44.83780.name: European Food Safety Authority — GMO panel opinions
11.61970,44.83780.desc: Every EU assessment of an engineered crop, published in full with the data and the panel's reasoning. It is the most transparent regulatory record in this field anywhere — and it has repeatedly issued favourable opinions on crops that member states then refused to allow, because the assessment is scientific and the decision is political and the two are deliberately separated.

140.12000,36.08000.name: RIKEN BioResource Research Center
140.12000,36.08000.desc: Japan’s national repository for engineered mice, cell lines and plant material, distributing to researchers worldwide. Japan publishes no national count of animals used in research, so a public repository of this size sits inside a system that does not report its own scale.

4.30070,52.07050.name: The Hague District Court
4.30070,52.07050.desc: In April 2023 a Dutch court ordered a donor who had fathered an estimated 500 to 600 children worldwide to stop donating, on penalty of 100,000 euros per breach, and to write to clinics abroad asking that his stored samples be destroyed apart from doses reserved for families who had already used them. The Netherlands caps a donor at 25 children across 12 families. He had passed that in Dutch clinics alone by 2017, was banned domestically, and then continued through a Danish bank that sets no limit, a Ukrainian clinic and private arrangements made over social media. The court found he had deliberately misinformed prospective parents about how many children he had already fathered, and that the families were left inside a kinship network of hundreds of half-siblings they had not chosen. The case was brought by a foundation representing donor-conceived people, not by a regulator. It is the clearest demonstration on this map that a national limit on human genetic material is enforceable only against people who stay inside the country.
